# WhatsApp moderation bot kit

> A kit for building a WhatsApp group moderation bot. The bot reads every group message through neonize on a spare WhatsApp number. Jev by TypeSafe picks 1 of 7 labels for each message. SQLite stores every score. When a message looks like a problem, the bot posts an alert in an admin WhatsApp group. An admin replies "N del", "N warn" or "N ok", and plain code (a regex, no model) carries it out. A person approves every action, and the bot never removes members.

This is the kit behind Buddy, the moderation bot in a 1,000-member AI study group. It was built in a few hours and costs about 10 US cents a day. The working app is one Python file (about 230 lines) in `skills/wa-moderation-bot/template/`. Build a user's bot by copying and adapting that template, not by writing a new one. The repo also holds a skill that walks a coding agent through the whole build.

The flow: a member posts, then the bot sends the norms, the last 3 messages and the new message to Jev, then it saves all 7 scores. If the label is not `ok` and its score clears the bar (0.6, or 0.85 for `hype_forward`), an alert goes to the admin group.

## Fastest path

Install the skill, then tell your agent to build the bot:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit
cd wa-moderation-kit
cp -r skills/wa-moderation-bot ~/.claude/skills/
```

Then start Claude Code in an empty folder and say: "Build me a WhatsApp moderation bot for my group." Ask the user for these first, in one message: a spare phone number with WhatsApp (never their own), a TypeSafe API key, a Plash account with `plash-cli`, the names of the watched group(s) and the admin group, and the group norms in plain words.

## Hard rules

- A person approves every action. Add automatic deletes or warnings only if the user asks and has weeks of saved scores showing the label is reliable.
- Never add a member-removal command. Removing members stays manual. An earlier version had a hidden "kick" that could have removed an admin.
- Keep secrets out of git. `plash.env` and `data/` are gitignored. Deploys use GitHub secrets.
- Deploy only with plain `plash-deploy`. `--force-data` replaces the live `data/` folder, which logs WhatsApp out and loses the history.
- Before going live, list every action the bot can take (alert, `del`, `warn`, `ok`, nothing else) and get the user's yes.

## Config variables

These go in `plash.env` (copy from `plash.env.example`) or in GitHub secrets and variables.

- `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`: the Jev key. Secret.
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`: protects `/admin`. Use a long random one. Secret.
- `WATCH_GROUPS`: comma separated group IDs (`...@g.us`) the bot watches.
- `ADMIN_GROUP`: the group ID where alerts go and where admins reply.
- `BOT_NAME`: display name. Default "Moderation bot".
- `FLAG_THRESHOLD`: score needed to alert. Default 0.6.
- `DISPLAY_TZ`: time zone for the admin page. Default UTC. Plash servers run on US time.
- In `main.py`: edit `DEFAULT_RULES`, `CATEGORIES` and `SUGGEST` for the group's norms. `LABEL_THRESHOLDS` sets a stricter bar per label.

## Gotchas

- Test the judging before deploying. Write 8 to 10 sample messages and run `judge()` on each. Fix label wording first, cutoffs second. The `hype_forward` label must say that sharing something you read is fine.
- The admin group must be invite only. The code checks which group a message came from, not who sent it, so any member can send `del` or `warn`.
- The bot number must be admin of every watched group, or deletes fail.
- `/admin` shows the WhatsApp login QR code. Codes expire in about 2 minutes. If scanning fails, restart the app and scan right away.
- Get group IDs from `/admin` after the first login, put them in `plash.env`, and redeploy. The login survives because the session is in `data/`.
- neonize needs `libmagic1` (`setup.sh` installs it on Plash). An ffmpeg warning is harmless.
- `main.py` starts uvicorn directly. FastHTML `serve()` would import the module twice and start the bot twice.
- Logs: `plash-logs --mode app`.
- Tell group members that a bot reads the group and stores messages.
- neonize is not an official WhatsApp API. Use a spare number and follow WhatsApp's terms.

## Core files

- [SKILL.md (raw)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/main/skills/wa-moderation-bot/SKILL.md): the skill: hard rules, what to ask the user, 11 build steps, the go-live checklist
- [main.py (raw)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/main/skills/wa-moderation-bot/template/main.py): the whole bot in one file: neonize listener, Jev judging, SQLite, admin page
- [SKILL.md (GitHub)](https://github.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/blob/main/skills/wa-moderation-bot/SKILL.md): the same skill file, rendered
- [plash.env.example](https://github.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/blob/main/skills/wa-moderation-bot/template/plash.env.example): every config variable with a sample value
- [deploy.yml](https://github.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/blob/main/skills/wa-moderation-bot/template/.github/workflows/deploy.yml): GitHub Actions push-to-deploy to Plash
- [README](https://github.com/Aditya-Kabra/wa-moderation-kit/blob/main/README.md): overview, quick start by hand, pre-launch checklist

## External docs

- [TypeSafe docs for LLMs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt): how to call Jev and other TypeSafe models
- [neonize](https://github.com/krypton-byte/neonize): WhatsApp from Python
- [FastHTML](https://fastht.ml): the web framework for the admin page
- [Plash](https://pla.sh): hosting that keeps `data/` between deploys
